```{r}
#| label: setup

# load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(tidycensus)
library(rnassqs)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(FedData)
library(exactextractr)
library(censusapi)

# set API keys
readRenviron("../.Renviron")
nassqs_auth(key = Sys.getenv('NASSQS_TOKEN'))
census_api_key(Sys.getenv('CENSUS_API_KEY'))

# county data
county_shapes <- tigris::counties("ID") %>%
  select(c("GEOID", "NAME")) %>%
  mutate(tot_area = st_area(.))

# workaround when tigris is down
# county_shapes <- st_read("/vsizip/R:/CarolynKoehn/Data_raw/US_county_2020.zip/US_county_2020.shp") %>%
#   filter(STATEFP == 16) %>%
#   select(GEOID, NAME) %>%
#   mutate(tot_area = st_area(.))

# names and GEOIDs
GEOID_names <- st_drop_geometry(county_shapes$NAME)
names(GEOID_names) <- st_drop_geometry(county_shapes$GEOID)
```

This document contains all code used to access and clean data for the clustering models. We downloaded a backup copy of all data accessed via API calls and recommend any users of this code do the same, as continued access to public databases is (unfortunately) never guaranteed.

# Resource System

```{r}
#| label: "RS data setup"

rs_data <- expand.grid(county = county_shapes$NAME, 
                        year = seq(1990, 2020, 10))
```


## RS3 -- Size of resource system

### Agriculture

#### Percent land in farms

Data for 2002-2022 are available through the USDA NASS API. Data for 1992 were digitized from https://web.archive.org/web/20250907173430/https://agcensus.library.cornell.edu/census_parts/1992-idaho/, Chapter 2, Table 6. 

```{r}
#| label: "percent land in farms"

# list NASS API search parameters
params <- list(agg_level_desc = "county",
               state_name = "Idaho",
               year = c(2002, 2012, 2022),
               short_desc = c("Farm operations - acres operated",
                              "Land area, incl non-ag - acres"),
               domain_desc = "total")

# query NASS API
land_in_farms <- nassqs(params)

# import and clean digitized historic data
land_in_farms_1992 <- read.csv("../data/perc_land_in_farms_ID_counties_1925-2022.csv") %>%
  filter(Year == 1992) %>%
  select(County, Year, Perc_land_in_farms) %>%
  rename("county" = "County",
         "year" = "Year",
         "land_in_farms" = "Perc_land_in_farms") %>%
  mutate(year = year-2)

# clean and join
rs_data <- land_in_farms %>%
  # pivot so that columns are county, year, land in farms area, and total county area
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(county_name, year),
              names_from = statisticcat_desc,
              values_from = Value) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  # calculate percent of county land in farms
  mutate(land_in_farms = `AREA OPERATED` / `AREA` * 100) %>%
  # clean for joining into resource system data.frame
  rename("county" = "county_name") %>%
  mutate(county = str_to_title(county),
         year = as.numeric(year)) %>%
  select(c(county, year, land_in_farms)) %>%
  mutate(year = (year-2)) %>%
  rbind(land_in_farms_1992) %>%
  # join into full RS data
  right_join(rs_data, by=c("county", "year"))
```

#### Percent cropland

NLCD data were downloaded from https://www.mrlc.gov/viewer/

```{r}
#| label: "load NLCD data"

# load a list of all raster files
file_list <- subset(unzip("../data/raw_data/NLCD_LndCov_1985-2020.zip", list=TRUE)$Name,
                    str_detect(unzip("../data/raw_data/NLCD_LndCov_1985-2020.zip", list=TRUE)$Name, "tiff$"))
# sort file list by year
file_list <- file_list[order(file_list)]

# read list of raster files into a stacked raster
nlcd_all_years_ID <- rast(paste0("/vsizip/../data/raw_data/NLCD_LndCov_1985-2020.zip/", file_list))
# add years as raster layer names
names(nlcd_all_years_ID) <- seq(1985,2020,5)

# following code modified from @canderson156 at https://gis.stackexchange.com/questions/425821/calculating-proportion-of-a-polygon-covered-by-each-raster-category-using-r

# function to total the percent of each category in a given area
sum_cover <- function(x){
  list(x %>%
    group_by(value) %>%
    summarize(total_area = sum(coverage_area)) %>%
    mutate(proportion = total_area/sum(total_area)))
  
}

# total proportion of each land cover in each county and year
land_cover_counts <- lapply(nlcd_all_years_ID, function(x) {
                            exact_extract(x = x,
                                   y = county_shapes,
                                   append_cols = "NAME",
                                   coverage_area = TRUE,
                                   summarize_df = TRUE,
                                   fun = sum_cover)
})

# end @canderson156 code

# organize into compatible data frame
names(land_cover_counts) <- names(nlcd_all_years_ID)

# pair land cover codes with category name in reference vector
group_recode <- c(nlcd_colors()$Class, use.names=TRUE)
names(group_recode) <- as.character(nlcd_colors()$ID)

land_cover_percents <- bind_rows(land_cover_counts, .id="year") %>%
  # add land cover label and convert from proportion to percent
  mutate(land_cover = recode(result.value, !!!group_recode),
         cover_percent = result.proportion*100) %>%
  rename("county" = "NAME") %>%
  select(county, year, land_cover, cover_percent) %>%
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year))
```

```{r}
#| label: "percent cropland"

cropland <- land_cover_percents %>%
  filter(land_cover %in% c("Pasture/Hay", "Cultivated Crops")) %>%
  group_by(county, year) %>%
  summarise(percent_cropland = sum(cover_percent))

rs_data <- left_join(rs_data, cropland, by=c("county", "year"))
```

#### Percent federal lands

The API call is the 2026 BLM Idaho Surface Management Agency (Surface Ownership) dataset, also available for download at https://gbp-blm-egis.hub.arcgis.com/pages/idaho or https://gbp-blm-egis.hub.arcgis.com/datasets/BLM-EGIS::blm-id-surface-management-agency/about. Federal lands are assumed to not be sold or acquired over the 40 year time period.

```{r}
#| label: "percent federal land"

# API call to BLM data repository, accessed 7/17/2025
id_lt <- st_read("https://gis.blm.gov/idarcgis/rest/services/lands/BLM_ID_Surface_Management_Agency/FeatureServer/0/query?outFields=*&where=1%3D1&f=geojson", quiet=TRUE) %>%
  # project to EPSG 4269
  st_transform(st_crs(county_shapes)) %>%
  # make polygons valid
  st_make_valid()

# create simpler tenure categories from agency names
id_lt$Simple_Tenure <- ifelse(id_lt$AGNCY_NAME == "PRIVATE", "Private",
                            ifelse(id_lt$AGNCY_NAME %in% c("BIA", "IR"), "Tribal",
                              ifelse(id_lt$AGNCY_NAME %in% c("OTHER", "HSTRCWTR"), "Other",
                                ifelse(str_starts(id_lt$AGNCY_NAME, "STATE"), "State", "Federal"))))
# filter to only federal lands
fed_clip <- id_lt %>%
  filter(Simple_Tenure == "Federal")
# remove non-polygons
fed_clip <- fed_clip[list(st_geometry_type(fed_clip))[[1]] %in% c("POLYGON", "MULTIPOLYGON"),]

# split federal land polygons along county lines
county_polys <- fed_clip %>% 
  st_intersection(., county_shapes) %>%
  st_make_valid()
# remove non-polygons
county_polys <- county_polys[list(st_geometry_type(county_polys))[[1]] %in% c("POLYGON", "MULTIPOLYGON"),]
    
# union federal land polygons within each county into multipolygons
county_polys <- county_polys %>%
  group_by(NAME) %>%
  dplyr::summarise() %>%
  st_make_valid()

# make copy of this data.frame for non-fed land near highways step later in document
fed_for_roads <- county_polys

fed_by_county <- county_polys %>%
    # calculate area of federal land in each county
    mutate(fed_area = st_area(.)) %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    # join with county info data.frame
    left_join(st_drop_geometry(county_shapes)) %>%
    # calculate percent federal land area
    mutate(perc_fed = units::drop_units(fed_area / tot_area * 100))

# clean and join to full RS data
rs_data <- fed_by_county %>%
  rename("county" = "NAME") %>%
  select("county", "perc_fed") %>%
  right_join(rs_data, by=c("county"))
```

#### Lake area

Data from the Hydrosheds HydroLAKES product were downloaded from https://www.hydrosheds.org/products/hydrolakes

```{r}
#| label: "percent open water"

# filter downloaded Hydrolakes data to the USA
us_lakes <- st_read("/vsizip/../data/raw_data/HydroLAKES_polys_v10_shp.zip/HydroLAKES_polys_v10_shp/HydroLAKES_polys_v10.shp") %>%
  filter(Country == "United States of America")

lakes_area <- us_lakes %>%
  # filter to approximate coordinates for Idaho
  filter(Pour_lat > 41 & Pour_lat < 50 &
           Pour_long > -118 & Pour_long < -110) %>%
  st_make_valid(.) %>%
  # split lake polygons along county lines
  st_intersection(st_transform(county_shapes, st_crs(.))) %>%
  group_by(NAME) %>%
  # union lake polygons within each county into multipolygons
  dplyr::summarise() %>%
  # calculate lake area in each county
  mutate(lake_area = st_area(.))
  

rs_data <- lakes_area %>%
  # conver lake area to km2 and then drop the units data item
  mutate(lake_area_km2 = units::drop_units(units::set_units(lake_area, "km2"))) %>%
  st_drop_geometry(.) %>%
  select(-lake_area) %>%
  rename("county" = "NAME") %>%
  # join to full RS data
  right_join(rs_data, by=c("county")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  # if no lakes, set lake area to 0 instead of NA
  mutate(lake_area_km2 = ifelse(is.na(lake_area_km2), 0, lake_area_km2))
```

#### Miles of river

WWF Hydrosheds data 
1. Was accessed on Google Earth Engine
2. Filtered to rivers of order 7 and lower (defined and calculated based on the long-term average discharge using logarithmic progression: * 1 = > 100000 * 2 = 10000 - 100000 * 3 = 1000 - 10000 * 4 = 100 - 1000 * 5 = 10 - 100 * 6 = 1 - 10 * 7 = 0.1 - 1 * 8 = 0.01 - 0.1 * 9 = 0.001 - 0.01 * 10 = < 0.001)
3. Cropped to Idaho
4. Downloaded and imported to R here

Google Earth Engine code can be found here: https://code.earthengine.google.com/9e6f18b96e72318dc90a7bdd48e50c4d

```{r}
#| label: "miles of river"

rivers <- st_read("/vsizip/../data/raw_data/ID_Rivers_ORD7.zip/ID_Rivers_ORD7.shp") %>%
  # project to EPSG 4269
  st_transform(st_crs(county_shapes)) %>%
  # split rivers along county lines
  st_intersection(county_shapes) %>%
  # calculate river lengths
  mutate(length = st_length(.)) %>%
  st_drop_geometry(.) %>%
  group_by(NAME) %>%
  # in each county, sum river length and divide by county area
  summarise(rivers_km_per_km2 = 
              sum(units::set_units(length, "km")) / mean(units::set_units(tot_area, "km2")))

# clean and join to full RS data
rs_data <- rivers %>%
  mutate(rivers_km_per_km2 = units::drop_units(rivers_km_per_km2)) %>%
  left_join(rs_data, ., by = c("county" = "NAME"))
```

```{r}
  group_by(county, year) %>%
```

### Urban Land

Since the definition of urban area changed for the 2020 census, we recreated urban areas for 1990-2020 with the 2020 definitions and thresholds. Urban definition here: https://www.census.gov/newsroom/blogs/random-samplings/2022/12/redefining-urban-areas-following-2020-census.html

Total population and housing units data for blocks in Idaho, 1990-2020, data downloaded from:
Steven Manson, Jonathan Schroeder, David Van Riper, Katherine Knowles, Tracy Kugler, Finn Roberts, and Steven Ruggles. IPUMS National Historical Geographic Information System: Version 19.0 [dataset]. Minneapolis, MN: IPUMS. 2024. http://doi.org/10.18128/D050.V19.0

```{r}
#| label: "urban land"

# create a polygon - Idaho + 150 miles of buffer
id_buff <- st_buffer(st_union(county_shapes), dist = units::set_units(150, "mi"))

#############
# get urban populations

# get names of IPUMS population and housing data files
censdata_files <- list.files(path = "../data/raw_data/nhgis0006_csv/nhgis0006_csv", 
                             pattern=".csv",
                             full.names = TRUE)
# create list with an element for each data file
censdata_list <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(censdata_files))
# read each data file into a different list element
for(i in 1:length(censdata_list)) {
  censdata_list[[i]] <- read.csv(censdata_files[i])
}

# get names of IPUMS census block polygon data files for each year
# files are zip files containing all census blocks for each year and each state (ID and all states within 150 miles of it)
blocks_zip_files <- list.files(path = "..", pattern="shapefile", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
# create list with an element for each data file
blocks_shp_files <- vector(mode = "character", length = length(blocks_zip_files))
# create vector of data import strings for each shapefile
for(i in 1:length(blocks_zip_files)) {
  blocks_shp_files[i] <- paste0("/vsizip/", 
                                blocks_zip_files[i], "/",
                                # detect name of shapefile within each zip file
                                filter(unzip(zipfile = blocks_zip_files[i], list=TRUE),
                                       str_detect(Name, ".shp$"))$Name)
}
# create list to hold all census blocks for each year in a different element
blocks_list <- vector(mode = "list", length = 4)
# create vector of years
years <- seq(1990, 2020, 10)
for(i in 1:length(blocks_list)) {
  # detect file names in blocks_shp_files with current year in loop
  year_files <- blocks_shp_files[str_detect(blocks_shp_files, 
                                            paste0(years[i], ".shp"))]
  # loop through detected elements in blocks_shp_files
  for(f in year_files) {
    # if it is the first detected file name
    if(f == year_files[1]) {
      # read shapefile into sf data.frame
      year_blocks <- st_read(f) %>%
        # select column with code for joining to population and housing data
        select(GISJOIN) %>%
        # create column with FIPS code for joining to tigris data (county_shapes)
        mutate(FIPS = paste0(str_sub(GISJOIN, 2, 3), str_sub(GISJOIN, 5, 7)))
    # if not the first detected file name
    } else {
      # add on to sf data.frame with same cleaning steps as above
      year_blocks <- st_read(f) %>%
        select(GISJOIN) %>%
        mutate(FIPS = paste0(str_sub(GISJOIN, 2, 3), str_sub(GISJOIN, 5, 7))) %>%
        rbind(year_blocks)
    }
  } # end data import
  
  # make poygons valid and crop to within 150 miles of Idaho
  blocks_list[[i]] <- year_blocks %>%
    st_make_valid(.) %>%
    filter(st_is_valid(.)) %>%
    st_filter(st_transform(id_buff, st_crs(.)))
}
# end result is a 4-element list
# each element is one year and contains all census blocks for that year from Idaho and within 150 miles of Idaho
# census block polygons are valid and in their native projection (USA Contiguous Albers Equal Area Conic)

# create function to join census data to census block polygons in each year
join_clean_cens_blocks <- function(censdata, blocks) {
  # save the column numbers of population and housing data (will vary with year)
  pop_col <- ncol(censdata)-1
  hous_col <- ncol(censdata)
  
  censdata %>%
    # rename population and housing columns to a standard name in each year
    rename("tot_pop" = pop_col,
           "hous_units" = hous_col) %>%
    select(GISJOIN, tot_pop, hous_units) %>%
    # join with census blocks data
    full_join(blocks, by = "GISJOIN") %>%
    # convert to sf object
    st_as_sf() %>%
    # create columns for total census block area and housing density by census block
    mutate(area_sq_mi = units::set_units(st_area(.), "mi2"),
           hous_dens = units::drop_units(hous_units / area_sq_mi)) %>%
    # make all census block polygons valid
    st_make_valid(.) %>%
    # filter out invalid or empty polygons
    filter(st_is_valid(.) & !st_is_empty(.))
}

block_data_list <- mapply(join_clean_cens_blocks, 
                          censdata = censdata_list, 
                          blocks = blocks_list,
                          SIMPLIFY = FALSE)
# end result is a 4-element list
# each element is one year and contains all census blocks for that year from Idaho and within 150 miles of Idaho, as well as their associated population and housing data
# census block polygons are valid and in their native projection (USA Contiguous Albers Equal Area Conic)

# remove large lists to free memory
rm(censdata_list)
rm(blocks_list)
rm(year_blocks)

# function that filters out rows with >= 425 housing units/sq mi -> inital urban core blocks
init_urban_core <- function(block_data) {
  block_data %>%
    filter(hous_dens >= 425)
}

# apply inital urban core blocks function to each year of block data
init_urban_core_list <- lapply(block_data_list, init_urban_core)

# function that fills out the urban areas by following criteria described in Appendix A.1.1.9
fill_urb_area <- function(init_urban_core, block_data) {
  # initialize the initial urban cores as the current urban area
  current_urb <- init_urban_core
  
  repeat {
    # find all blocks adjacent to current urban area
    neighbors <- st_intersects(current_urb, block_data)
    # get row index of neighboring blocks
    nb_idx <- unique(unlist(neighbors))
    # add blocks with >200 houses/mi2 to new urban area
    new_urb <- block_data[nb_idx, ] %>%
      filter(hous_dens >= 200) %>%
      rbind(current_urb) %>%
      # filter out any repeated rows
      distinct()
  
    # break loop if current and new urban area are the same
    # no blocks with high enough housing density were adjacent
    if(nrow(current_urb) == nrow(new_urb)) {
      break
    } else {
      # otherwise rewrite the new urban area as the current urban area and repeat loop
      current_urb <- new_urb
    }
  }
  
  return(new_urb)
}

# apply fill urban areas function to each year
urb_areas_list <- mapply(fill_urb_area,
                         init_urban_core = init_urban_core_list,
                         block_data = block_data_list,
                         SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

# free memory
rm(init_urban_core_list)

# function to filter out urban areas without a dense urban core
urb_areas_thresholded <- function(urb_areas, block_data) {
  # melt all boundaries between urban blocks
  urb_union <- st_union(urb_areas)
  # separate the unioned multipolygon into separate urban area polygons
  urb_union_polys <- st_cast(urb_union, "POLYGON")
  
  # identify which urban area each block is covered by (if any)
  # returns list where each item represents a block and contains the urban area index it is part of
  blocks_covered <- st_covered_by(block_data, urb_union_polys)
  # identify which blocks (rows) meet our high density criteria
  high_dens_nucleus <- which(block_data$hous_dens >= 1275)
  # return the urban area indices belonging to high density blocks
  high_dens_blocks <- blocks_covered[high_dens_nucleus]
  # get row numbers of urban areas that have high density blocks
  high_dens_poly_idx <- unique(unlist(high_dens_blocks))
  # filter urban areas to only return those associated with high density block(s)
  urb_area_polys <- urb_union_polys[high_dens_poly_idx]

  # reassign blocks to urban/non-urban based on new areas
  new_blocks_covered <- st_covered_by(block_data, urb_area_polys)
  # return list of labels for each block: non-urban = NA, urban = index of urban area
  new_blocks_covered <- lapply(new_blocks_covered, function(x) {
    if(length(x) == 0) {
      return(NA)
    } else {
      return(x)
    }
  })
  
  # filter out urban areas with low total houses or population
  urb_areas_filt <- block_data %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    # add column with urban labels
    mutate(in_urb_area = unlist(new_blocks_covered)) %>%
    # group by urban labels
    group_by(in_urb_area) %>%
    # calculate total houses and population in each area
    summarise(pop_thres = sum(tot_pop),
              hous_thres = sum(hous_units)) %>%
    # apply filter
    filter(pop_thres >= 5000 | hous_thres >= 2000)

    # return urban area polygons that meet both criteria
    return(urb_area_polys[urb_areas_filt$in_urb_area])
}

# apply thresholding function to each year
urb_areas_thresholded_list <- mapply(urb_areas_thresholded,
                                     urb_areas = urb_areas_list,
                                     block_data = block_data_list,
                                     SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

# free memory
rm(urb_areas_list)

# apply a distance from urban label to each block
block_data_list <- mapply(function(x, y) {
  # new column with NA label for each block
  x$dist_from_urb <- NA
  
  # return vector with label - if block is in an urban area (T/F)
  in_urb_area <- as.logical(
    rowSums(
      st_covered_by(x, y, sparse = FALSE)
      )
    )
  
  # if block is in urban area, dist from urb = 0
  x$dist_from_urb <- ifelse(is.na(x$dist_from_urb) & in_urb_area == TRUE, 0, NA)
  
  print("Urban blocks labelled")
  
  # initialize a tracker object for loop
  miles <- 10
  repeat {
    # buffer each urban area by _miles_ miles and determine which blocks are covered
    urb_area_dist <- as.logical(
      rowSums(
        st_covered_by(x, st_union(st_buffer(y, units::set_units(miles, "mi"))), sparse = FALSE)
        )
      )
    
    if(any(is.na(x$dist_from_urb)) & miles <= 100) {
      # apply appropriate label to blocks currently with NA label
      x$dist_from_urb <- ifelse(is.na(x$dist_from_urb) & urb_area_dist == TRUE, 
                                miles, x$dist_from_urb)
      
      print(paste("Blocks within", miles, "miles of urban area labelled"))
      # advance tracer object and repeat cycle
      miles <- miles + 10
    # if miles > 100, apply ">100" label and break loop
    } else {
      x$dist_from_urb <- ifelse(is.na(x$dist_from_urb), 
                                ">100", x$dist_from_urb)
      
      print("Item compete")
      break
    }
  }
  
  # return blocks data now with urban labels
  return(x)
}, x = block_data_list, y = urb_areas_thresholded_list, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

# calculate area of coverage of each dist from urban category in each county
urb_dist_areas <- mapply(function(df, year) {
  df %>%
    # filter to only blocks in Idaho
    filter(str_starts(FIPS, "16")) %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    # join with county data
    left_join(st_drop_geometry(county_shapes), by = c("FIPS" = "GEOID")) %>%
    # group by county and dist from urb category
    group_by(NAME, dist_from_urb) %>%
    # calculate sum of census block area in each dist from urb category
    summarise(area = sum(area_sq_mi),
              # retain total county area
              tot_area = mean(tot_area)) %>%
    # percent area of each dist from urb category in each county
    mutate(perc_area = units::drop_units(area / units::set_units(tot_area, "mi2")) * 100) %>%
    select(-c(area, tot_area)) %>%
    # pivot so counties are rows and each dist from urb category is a column with percentages
    pivot_wider(id_cols = "NAME",
                names_from = "dist_from_urb",
                names_prefix = "dist_from_urb",
                values_from = "perc_area",
                # any dist from urb categories not present in a county = 0%
                values_fill = 0) %>%
    # add year label to data
    mutate(year = year)
}, df = block_data_list, year = years)
# returns a list with counties and their distance from urban composition for each year

# combine list into one data.frame
urb_dist_areas <- do.call(rbind, urb_dist_areas) %>%
  # fill all missing cells with 0 if not filled already
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ifelse(is.na(.x), 0, .x))) %>%
  # organize column order
  relocate(year, .after = NAME) %>%
  rename("county" = "NAME") 

# perform PCA for distance to urban composition data
urb_dist_pca <- prcomp(urb_dist_areas[,-c(1:2)])

# PC1 and PC2 account for >75% of variance
rs_data <- cbind(urb_dist_areas[,1:2], urb_dist_pca$x[,c("PC1", "PC2")]) %>%
  rename("urb_dist_pc1" = "PC1",
         "urb_dist_pc2" = "PC2") %>%
  right_join(rs_data, by = c("county", "year"))
```

## RS4 -- Human-constructed facilities

### Agriculture

#### Number farms per unit area

Data for 2002-2022 are available through the USDA NASS API. Data for 1992 were digitized from https://web.archive.org/web/20250907173430/https://agcensus.library.cornell.edu/census_parts/1992-idaho/, Chapter 2, Table 6.

```{r}
#| label: "number farms per unit area"

# list API parameters
params <- list(agg_level_desc = "county",
               state_name = "Idaho",
               year = c(2002, 2012, 2022),
               short_desc = c("Farm operations - number of operations",
                              "Land area, incl non-ag - acres"),
               domain_desc = "total")

# query QuickStats API
num_farms <- nassqs(params)

# retrieve and clean 1990 data for num farms and total land area
num_farms_1992 <- read.csv("../data/Farm_size_1925-1992.csv") %>%
  filter(Year == 1992 & Size == "all farms") %>%
  left_join(read.csv("../data/perc_land_in_farms_ID_counties_1925-2022.csv")) %>%
  # calculate farm density
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(farms_per_acre = Num_farms / Total_county_land_acres) %>%
  select(County, Year, farms_per_acre) %>%
  rename("county" = "County",
         "year" = "Year") %>%
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year-2))

# clean and join
rs_data <- num_farms %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(county_name, year),
              names_from = statisticcat_desc,
              values_from = Value) %>%
  # calculate farm density
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(farms_per_acre = `OPERATIONS` / `AREA`) %>%
  rename("county" = "county_name") %>%
  mutate(county = str_to_title(county),
         year = as.numeric(year)) %>%
  select(c(county, year, farms_per_acre)) %>%
  mutate(year = (year-2)) %>%
  rbind(num_farms_1992) %>%
  right_join(rs_data, by=c("county", "year"))
```

### Natural Amenities

#### Recreation Units

PAD-US 4.1 data were downloaded from https://www.usgs.gov/programs/gap-analysis-project/science/pad-us-data-download. The Protected Areas Database "was originally designed to support biodiversity assessments; however, its scope expanded in recent years to include all public and nonprofit held lands and waters." ([source](https://www.usgs.gov/programs/gap-analysis-project/pad-us-data-manual)). 

The following land designations were considered "recreation lands" to calculate percent recreation land in this analysis: Recreation Management Area, National Monument, National Park, State Recreation Area, State Park, National Recreation Area, National Scenic or Historic Trail. Additional local designation terms related to recreation were added as well, as some state parks were misclassified as `LP` (local parks) in the `Des_Tp` (designation type) column.

We also use Euclidean distance to calculate distance to national parks and ski areas within 100km.

```{r}
#| label: "percent recreation lands"

# read in PAD-US data
padus <- st_read("/vsizip/../data/raw_data/PADUS4_1Geodatabase.zip/PADUS4_1Geodatabase.gdb", 
                 layer = "PADUS4_1Combined_Proclamation_Marine_Fee_Designation_Easement") %>%
  # filter to Idaho and surrounding states
  filter(State_Nm %in% c("ID", "WA", "OR", "WY", "UT", "NV", "MT")) %>%
  # filter out invalid polygons
  filter(st_is_valid(.))

pad_rec <- padus %>%
  # filter to only lands in study area counties
  st_filter(st_transform(county_shapes, st_crs(.))) %>%
  # filter to only "recreation land" types described above this code chunk
  filter(Des_Tp %in% c("REC", "NM", "NP", "SREC", "SP", "NRA", "NT") |
           Loc_Ds %in% c("State Park", "Recreation Reservoir", "National Recreation Trail", "Recreation Area", "National Recreation Area", "National Monument", "SREC", "REC", "SP", "National Park", "Designated - Recreational"))

# create a labeled empty list with one item for each year
pad_rec_years <- vector("list", length=4)
names(pad_rec_years) <- seq(1990, 2020, 10)

# for each year:
pad_rec_years <- mapply(function(list, year) {
  county_polys <- pad_rec %>% 
    # filter to only recreation lands established that year or before
    filter(Date_Est <= year | is.na(Date_Est)) %>%
    # split rec lands by county lines
    st_intersection(., st_transform(county_shapes, st_crs(.))) %>%
    # make all rec land polygons valid
    st_make_valid()
  # keep only rec lands that are polygons (no points or lines)
  county_polys <- county_polys[list(st_geometry_type(county_polys))[[1]] %in% c("POLYGON", "MULTIPOLYGON"),]
    
  county_polys <- county_polys %>%
    # group rec lands by county
    group_by(NAME) %>%
    # melt rec lands in each county into one multipolygon
    dplyr::summarise() %>%
    # make rec land multipolygons valid
    st_make_valid()
}, list = pad_rec_years, year = seq(1990, 2020, 10), SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

# for each year:
rec_by_county_years <- lapply(pad_rec_years, function(df) {
  df %>%
    # calculate total area of rec lands in each county
    mutate(rec_area = st_area(.)) %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    # join with county data
    left_join(st_drop_geometry(county_shapes)) %>%
    # calculate percent rec lands compared to total county land
    mutate(perc_rec = units::drop_units(rec_area / tot_area * 100))
})

# clean and join
# bind rows of list items into single data.frame
rs_data <- bind_rows(rec_by_county_years, .id="year") %>%
  rename("county" = "NAME") %>%
  select("county", "year", "perc_rec") %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) %>%
  right_join(rs_data, by=c("county", "year")) %>%
  # convert NAs to 0% rec land
  mutate(perc_rec = ifelse(is.na(perc_rec), 0, perc_rec))
```

```{r}
#| label: "distance to major recreation lands - national parks"

# filter PAD-US data to only ski areas and national parks
pad_ski_np <- padus %>%
  filter(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Ski ") | Des_Tp == "NP" | str_detect(Unit_Nm, "National Park"))

###### Euclidean distance to nearest national park

# identify closest national park to each county
np_nn <- st_nearest_feature(st_transform(county_shapes, st_crs(pad_ski_np)),
                          subset(pad_ski_np, !str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Ski "))) # subset the national park and ski data to only national parks (no "Ski ")
# calculate Euclidean distance to nearest national park
np_distance <- st_distance(st_transform(county_shapes, st_crs(pad_ski_np)),
                           subset(pad_ski_np, !str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Ski "))[np_nn,],
                           by_element = TRUE) %>%
  units::set_units(., "km")

# add county name labels, will in in correct order since they were used in the st_distance function
np_distance <- data.frame(dist_to_NP = np_distance,
                          county = county_shapes$NAME) %>%
  mutate(dist_to_NP = as.numeric(dist_to_NP))

# join
rs_data <- left_join(rs_data, np_distance, by = "county")
```

```{r}
#| label: "distance to major recreation lands - ski areas"

# create buffer around counties to use only ski areas within 100km of study area
counties_buff <- st_buffer(county_shapes, units::set_units(100, "km")) %>%
  st_transform(st_crs(pad_ski_np))

# manual date correction - when people started using the ski area, not when established officially as a "ski area"
# info sources for each manual date adjustment are listed
ski_areas <- subset(pad_ski_np, str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Ski")) %>%
  # filter to only ski areas within 100km of study area
  st_filter(counties_buff) %>%
  # https://skilookout.com/history-of-lookout
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Lookout Pass"), 1941, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://www.montanaliving.com/blogs/people/ski-visionaries-of-montana-discovery-basin
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Discovery Basin"), 1984, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://losttrail.com/about-lost-trail/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Lost Trail"), 1967, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://southwestmt.com/specialfeatures/this-is-montana/ski-areas/maverick-mountain/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Maverick Mountain"), 1946, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://visitmt.com/listing/turner-mountain
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Turner Mountain"), 1960, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://fremontcountyhistoricalsociety.org/article/bear-gulch-ski-basin
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Bear Basin"), 1939, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://fromboise.com/posts/the-history-of-bogus-basin
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Bogus Basin"), 1942, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://brundage.com/media/history/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Brundage Mountain"), 1961, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://www.grandtarghee.com/plan-your-trip/discover/about-targhee/history-of-targhee
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Grand Targhee"), 1966, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://www.jacksonhole.com/history
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Jackson Hole"), 1964, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://rexburgfun.com/kelly-canyon-ski-resort/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Kelly Canyon"), 1957, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://mccallskiheritagefoundation.org/mccall-ski-history/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Little Ski Hill"), 1937, Date_Est)) %>%
  # "Ski resort set for big season". Spokane Daily Chronicle. (Washington). Associated Press. November 23, 1951. p. 8.
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Magic Mountain"), 1951, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://www.idahostatejournal.com/news/local/tales-from-the-rock-local-riders-and-employees-recount-memories-as-pebble-creek-celebrates-75/article_ee54f6e0-d11e-11ee-bd6c-5b2de0909f20.html
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Pebble Creek"), 1949, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://www.kivitv.com/news/outdoors/pomerelle-mountain-resort-features-a-unique-mix-of-elevation-history-and-family-vibes
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Pomerelle"), 1940, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://snowkingmountain.com/discover-snow-king/snow-king-mountain-resort-history/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Snow King"), 1946, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://www.snowbasin.com/about/history/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Snowbasin"), 1940, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://soldiermountain.com/about/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Soldier Mountain"), 1947, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://visitsunvalley.com/about-sun-valley/history/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Sun Valley"), 1936, Date_Est))

###### Euclidean distance to nearest ski area

# create empty labeled list with item for each year
pad_ski_years <- vector("list", length=4)
names(pad_ski_years) <- seq(1990, 2020, 10)

# for each year:
pad_ski_years <- mapply(function(list, year) {
  # did not need to filter by established date, all ski areas used before 1990
  # thus distance to ski is time invariant and the mapply is not necessary
  # I left the structure here in case it is needed with added data
  
  # identify nearest ski area for each county
  ski_nn <- st_nearest_feature(st_transform(county_shapes, st_crs(ski_areas)),
                          ski_areas)
  # find Euclidean distance to nearest ski area for each county (0 if contained in county)
  ski_distance <- st_distance(st_transform(county_shapes, st_crs(ski_areas)),
                           ski_areas[ski_nn,],
                           by_element = TRUE) %>%
  units::set_units("km")
  # add county name labels, will in in correct order since they were used in the st_distance function
  ski_distance <- data.frame(dist_to_ski = ski_distance,
                             county = county_shapes$NAME) %>%
  mutate(dist_to_ski = as.numeric(dist_to_ski))
  
  return(ski_distance)
}, list = pad_ski_years, year = seq(1990, 2020, 10), SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

# clean and join
rs_data <- bind_rows(pad_ski_years, .id="year") %>%
  select("county", "year", "dist_to_ski") %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) %>%
  right_join(rs_data, by=c("county", "year"))
```

### Residential

#### Number houses per unit area

Data for 2000-2020 were downloaded via `tidycensus`. Data for 1990 were digitized from https://www2.census.gov/library/publications/decennial/1990/cph-2/cph-2-14.pdf (available at https://www.census.gov/library/publications/1992/dec/cph-2.html)

```{r}
#| label: "number houses per unit area"

# read in 1990 data
houses1990 <- read.csv("../data/1990_US_Census_data.csv")
# retrieve and clean 2000 data
houses2000 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "H001001",
                        year = 2000) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))
# retrieve and clean 2010 data
houses2010 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "H001001",
                        year = 2010) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))
# retrieve and clean 2020 data
houses2020 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "H1_001N",
                        year = 2020) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))

# get county areas from digitized Census of Ag data
county_areas <- read.csv("../data/perc_land_in_farms_ID_counties_1925-2022.csv") %>%
  filter(Year >= 1990) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(Year-2)) %>%
  select(County, Year, Total_county_land_acres)

# join census data
housing_units <- data.frame(county = c(houses1990$County,
                                       houses2000$NAME,
                                       houses2010$NAME,
                                       houses2020$NAME),
                            year = rep(seq(1990, 2020, 10), each = nrow(houses1990)),
                            housing_units = c(houses1990$Housing_Units,
                                              houses2000$value,
                                              houses2010$value,
                                              houses2020$value)) %>%
  # join to county area data
  left_join(county_areas,
            by = c("county" = "County",
                   "year" = "Year")) %>%
  # calculate houses per acre
  mutate(housing_units_per_acre = housing_units / Total_county_land_acres) %>%
  select(county, year, housing_units_per_acre)

# join
rs_data <- left_join(rs_data, housing_units)
```

### Access to highway

We used the tigris package to access primary and secondary road shapefiles from the US Census TIGER/Line shapefiles. Primary roads “are generally divided limited-access highways within the Federal interstate highway system or under state management,” and secondary roads are “main arteries, usually in the U.S. highway, state highway, or county highway system” (U.S. Census Bureau, 2024). 

```{r}
#| label: "access to highway"

# retrieve primary (interstate highways) and secondary (state highways, other major roads) roads from the census
ps_roads <- tigris::primary_secondary_roads(state="ID")

# buffer all major roads by 10 km
ps_roads_buff <- st_buffer(ps_roads, units::set_units(10, "km"))

######### subtract land in federal from all land by highways

# create template data.frame for holding road areas for each county
road_areas <- data.frame(county = GEOID_names,
                         tot_road_area = NA,
                         fed_road_area = NA)
# for each county:
for(c in GEOID_names) {
  # get only road buffer area in that county
  roads_by_county <- st_intersection(ps_roads_buff, 
                                     st_transform(subset(county_shapes, NAME == c),
                                                  st_crs(ps_roads_buff)))
  # get only road buffer area that is also federal land
  roads_by_county_fed <- st_intersection(ps_roads_buff, 
                                         st_transform(subset(fed_for_roads, 
                                                             NAME == c),
                                                      st_crs(ps_roads_buff)))
  # clean and combine both buffer areas
  combined_all <- roads_by_county %>%
    st_make_valid() %>%
    st_union(.) %>%
    st_make_valid()
  combined_fed <- roads_by_county_fed %>%
    st_make_valid() %>%
    st_union(.) %>%
    st_make_valid()
  
  # calculate total buffer area near roads
  road_areas[which(road_areas$county == c), "tot_road_area"] <-
    sum(units::set_units(st_area(combined_all), "km^2"))
  # caluculate total road buffer area that is federal land
  road_areas[which(road_areas$county == c), "fed_road_area"] <-
    sum(units::set_units(st_area(combined_fed), "km^2"))
}

road_areas <- road_areas %>%
  # join with county data
  full_join(st_drop_geometry(county_shapes), by = c("county" = "NAME")) %>%
  # subtract road buffer area in federal lands from total road buffer area
  mutate(non_fed_land_near_highway_km2 = tot_road_area - fed_road_area,
         # find percent of non-federal road buffer area compared to total county area
         perc_non_fed_road_area_km2 = units::drop_units(non_fed_land_near_highway_km2 / units::set_units(tot_area, "km^2") * 100))

# join to full resource data
rs_data <- rs_data %>%
  left_join(road_areas[,c("county", "perc_non_fed_road_area_km2")])
```

#### Healthcare workers

County Business Patterns reports private sector employment, but they sometimes add missing values for confidentiality. We used imputed missing values for 1997-2012 from:

Fabian Eckert, Teresa C. Fort, Peter K. Schott, and Natalie J. Yang. "Imputing Missing Values in the US Census Bureau's County Business Patterns." NBER Working Paper #26632, 2021. https://www.fpeckert.me/cbp/

2022 County Business Patterns data was downloaded with the `censusapi` package. NAICS codes were referenced here: https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/cbp/technical-documentation/reference/naics-descriptions.html

For public sector health workers, we used data from the Annual Survey of Public Employment & Payroll.

```{r}
#| label: "healthcare"

# associate GEOIDS with long string labels for 1997 public employment data
loc_emp_1997_labs <- read.table("../data/raw_data/employment/97CEMPID.DAT",
                                sep = ";", comment.char = "", quote = "") %>%
  # filter to Idaho
  filter(str_starts(V1, "13")) %>%
  # extract ID and GEOID from string label
  mutate(id = substr(V1, 1, 14),
         GEOID = substr(V1, 110, 114)) %>%
  select(-V1)
# read in 1997 public employment data
pub_health_1997 <- read_table("../data/raw_data/employment/97CEMPST.DAT",
                           na = "999999999",
                           col_names = c("id", "gov_func_code", "full_time_emp", "full_time_payroll", "part_time_emp", "part_time_payroll", "part_time_hours", "full_time_equivalent_emp")) %>%
  # filter to Idaho

  filter(gov_func_code %in% c("032", "040") & GEOID != "16   ") %>%
  group_by(GEOID) %>%

  summarise(pub_health_workers = sum(full_time_emp, part_time_emp, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%

  filter(NAICS2017 %in% c("621111", "621610", "622", "623")) %>%
  # add GEOID and year labels
  mutate(GEOID = paste0(state, county),
         year = 2022) %>%
  group_by(GEOID, year) %>%
  # add health workers together
  summarise(heath_workers = sum(EMP))

# combine private health workers data
priv_healthworkers <- do.call(rbind, list(healthcare9712, healthcare2022))

# join private and public health workers
healthworkers <- full_join(priv_healthworkers, pub_health_1997, by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  full_join(pub_health_2002, by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  full_join(pub_health_2012, by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  full_join(pub_health_2022, by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # add all health workers together
  mutate(health_workers = rowSums(.[3:ncol(.)], na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  # add county and year labels to match other resource data
  mutate(county = recode(GEOID, !!!GEOID_names),
         year = ifelse(year==1997, 1990, year-2)) %>%
  select(county, year, health_workers)

# get population (more info in actors section)
pop1990 <- read.csv("../data/raw_data/cencounts.csv") %>%
  select(pop1990, name) %>%
  filter(str_starts(name, "ID") & name != "ID Idaho") %>%
  mutate(name = str_remove(name, "ID "),
         name = str_remove(name, " County"))
pop2000 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "P001001",
                        year = 2000) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))
pop2010 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "P001001",
                        year = 2010) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))
pop2020 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "P1_001N",
                        year = 2020) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))

pop <- data.frame(county = c(pop1990$name,
                                  pop2000$NAME,
                                  pop2010$NAME,
                                  pop2020$NAME),
                            year = rep(seq(1990, 2020, 10), each = nrow(pop1990)),
                            pop = c(pop1990$pop1990,
                                    pop2000$value,
                                    pop2010$value,
                                    pop2020$value))

# join population and health workers
health_pop <- left_join(pop, healthworkers, by = c("county", "year")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  # replace NA health workers with 0
  mutate(healthworkers = ifelse(is.na(health_workers), 0, health_workers),
         pop = as.integer(pop)) %>%
  # calculate health workers per 1000 people
  mutate(healthworkers_per_1000 = healthworkers / (pop/1000))

# join to resource data
rs_data <- health_pop %>%
  select(county, year, healthworkers_per_1000) %>%
  right_join(rs_data, by = c("county", "year"))
```

## RS9 - Location

### All

#### Average slope

I tested a PCA of mean, median, max, and stdev of slope and range of elevations, and it correlated pretty closely to mean slope (cor: 0.978883), so only mean slope is used in the analysis.

```{r}
#| label: "slope"

# access elevation data
elevation <- elevatr::get_elev_raster(st_transform(county_shapes, 5070), z=9, clip="locations")

# calculate slope from elevation
slope <- terrain(elevation, v="slope", unit="degrees")

# calculate average slope by county
avg_slope <- exact_extract(slope, county_shapes, fun="mean", append_cols = "NAME") %>%
  rename("avg_slope" = "mean")

rs_data <- left_join(rs_data, avg_slope, by = c("county" = "NAME"))
```


```{r}
#| label: "save RS data"

write.csv(rs_data,
          "../data/RS_data.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```

## RU2 -- Growth or replacement rate

### Agriculture

#### Percent change in number of farms

Percent growth or decline compared to the number of farms 5 years previous. Data for 1997-2022 were downloaded from the NASS API. Data for 1987-1992 were digitized from https://agcensus.library.cornell.edu/census_parts/1992-idaho/, Chapter 2, Table 6. (This URL is no longer supported, use archive.org to see the archived version of this webpage.)

```{r}
#| label: "num farms change"

# read in digitized data
num_farms_1992_1987 <- read.csv("../data/Farm_size_1925-1992.csv") %>%
  filter(Year %in% c(1987, 1992) & Size == "all farms") %>%
  select(County, Year, Num_farms) %>%
  rename("county" = "County",
         "year" = "Year") %>%
  # match year to other data
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year-2))

# list parameters for NASS API query
params <- list(agg_level_desc = "county",
               state_name = "Idaho",
               year__GE = 1997,
               short_desc = "Farm operations - number of operations",
               domain_desc = "total")

# query NASS API
num_farms_change <- nassqs(params)

farm_change <- num_farms_change %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(county_name, year),
              names_from = statisticcat_desc,
              values_from = Value) %>%
  rename("county" = "county_name",
         "Num_farms" = "OPERATIONS") %>%
  mutate(county = str_to_title(county),
         year = as.numeric(year)) %>%
  select(c(county, year, Num_farms)) %>%
  # match year to other data
  mutate(year = (year-2)) %>%
  # add data from 1987-1992
  rbind(num_farms_1992_1987) %>%
  # sort by county and year
  arrange(county, year) %>%
  # take difference between farms at t(-5) and t(0)
  mutate(num_farms_prev = lag(Num_farms, 1),
         farm_change = Num_farms - num_farms_prev,
         perc_farms_change = farm_change / num_farms_prev * 100) %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1990,2000,2010,2020)) %>%
  select(county, year, perc_farms_change)

# join
ru_data <- left_join(ru_data, farm_change)
```

#### Change in land in farms

```{r}
#| label: "percent change land in farms"

# read in digitized data
land_in_farms_change <- read.csv("../data/perc_land_in_farms_ID_counties_1925-2022.csv") %>%
  # filter for years after or on 1987
  filter(Year >= 1987) %>%
  # sort by county and year
  arrange(County, Year) %>%
  # add lagged column with number of farms 5 years previous
  mutate(land_in_farms_lag = lag(Perc_land_in_farms)) %>%
  # filter to only years of analysis
  filter(Year %in% c(1992, 2002, 2012, 2022)) %>%
  # calculate difference in farms t(-5) and t(0)
  mutate(Perc_change_land_in_farms = Perc_land_in_farms - land_in_farms_lag) %>%
  select(County, Year, Perc_change_land_in_farms) %>%
  rename("county" = "County",
         "year" = "Year") %>%
  mutate(year = year-2)

# clean and join
ru_data <- left_join(ru_data, land_in_farms_change, by = c("county", "year"))
```

#### Change in cropland

```{r}
#| label: "cropland change"

cropland_change <- land_cover_percents %>%
  filter(land_cover %in% c("Pasture/Hay", "Cultivated Crops")) %>%
  group_by(county, year) %>%
  summarise(cover_percent = sum(cover_percent)) %>%
  arrange(county, year) %>%
  # create lagged column with cropland 5 years previous
  mutate(cropland_prev = lag(cover_percent, 1),
         # calculate difference
         cropland_change = cover_percent - cropland_prev,
         perc_cropland_change = cropland_change / cropland_prev * 100) %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1990,2000,2010,2020)) %>%
  select(county, year, cropland_change)

# join
ru_data <- left_join(ru_data, cropland_change)
```

```{r}
  group_by(county, year) %>%
  summarise(cover_percent = sum(cover_percent)) %>%
  arrange(county, year) %>%
  # create lagged column with forest 5 years previous
  mutate(forest_prev = lag(cover_percent, 1),

  mutate(shrub_prev = lag(cover_percent, 1),

         shrub_change = cover_percent - shrub_prev,
         perc_shrub_change = shrub_change / shrub_prev * 100) %>%
```

### Residential

#### Change in developed land

```{r}
#| label: "developed change"

developed_change <- land_cover_percents %>%
  filter(land_cover %in% c("Developed, Open Space", "Developed, Low Intensity", "Developed, Medium Intensity", "Developed High Intensity")) %>%
  group_by(county, year) %>%
  summarise(cover_percent = sum(cover_percent)) %>%
  arrange(county, year) %>%
  # create lagged column with developed land 5 years previous
  mutate(developed_prev = lag(cover_percent, 1),
         # calculate difference
         developed_change = cover_percent - developed_prev,
         perc_developed_change = developed_change / developed_prev * 100) %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1990,2000,2010,2020)) %>%
  select(county, year, developed_change)

# join
ru_data <- left_join(ru_data, developed_change)

# replace missing land change with 0%
ru_data <- ru_data %>%
  mutate(across(cropland_change:developed_change, ~ifelse(is.na(.x), 0, .x)))
```

## RU4 -- Economic value

### Agriculture

#### Farms with net loss

Data for 2002-2022 were downloaded from the NASS API. Data for 1992 were digitized from https://agcensus.library.cornell.edu/census_parts/1992-idaho/, Chapter 2, Table 4. (This URL is no longer supported, use archive.org to see archived version.)

```{r}
#| label: "farms with loss"

# list parameters for NASS API query
params <- list(agg_level_desc = "county",
               state_name = "Idaho",
               year = c(2002, 2012, 2022),
               short_desc = c("Income, net cash farm, of operations - operations with loss",
                              "Farm operations - number of operations"),
               domain_desc = "total")

# query NASS API
farms_w_loss <- nassqs(params)

# read in digitized data
farms_w_loss_1992 <- read.csv("../data/1992_CensOfAg_data.csv") %>%
  # join with digitized total farms data
  left_join(read.csv("../data/Farm_size_1925-1992.csv")) %>%
  filter(Size == "all farms") %>%
  # calculate percent farms with net loss
  mutate(perc_farms_w_net_loss = Farms_w_net_losses / Num_farms * 100) %>%
  rename("county" = "County",
         "year" = "Year") %>%
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year-2)) %>%
  select(county, year, perc_farms_w_net_loss)

# clean and join
ru_data <- farms_w_loss %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(county_name, year),
              names_from = statisticcat_desc,
              values_from = Value) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  # calculate percent farms with net loss
  mutate(perc_farms_w_net_loss = `LOSS` / `OPERATIONS` * 100) %>%
  rename("county" = "county_name") %>%
  mutate(county = str_to_title(county),
         # match year to other data
         year = as.numeric(year)-2) %>%
  select(c(county, year, perc_farms_w_net_loss)) %>%
  # join with 1992 data
  rbind(farms_w_loss_1992) %>%
  # join with resource data
  right_join(ru_data, by=c("county", "year"))
```

#### Jobs in agricultural support (hired labor, farm support services)

County Business Patterns reports private sector employment, but they sometimes add missing values for confidentiality. We used imputed missing values for 1997-2012 from:

Fabian Eckert, Teresa C. Fort, Peter K. Schott, and Natalie J. Yang. "Imputing Missing Values in the US Census Bureau's County Business Patterns." NBER Working Paper #26632, 2021. https://www.fpeckert.me/cbp/

2022 County Business Patterns data was downloaded with the `censusapi` package. NAICS codes were referenced here: https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/cbp/technical-documentation/reference/naics-descriptions.html

Hired labor was downloaded from the Census of Ag. Data for 1992 were digitized from https://agcensus.library.cornell.edu/wp-content/uploads/1992-Idaho-CHAPTER_2_County_Data-1570-Table-05.pdf (URL no longer supported, use archive.org)

```{r}
#| label: "ag jobs"

# read in digitized data on hired ag workers
hired1990 <- read.csv("../data/1992_CensOfAg_data.csv") %>%
  # match years
  mutate(year = as.integer(Year)-2) %>%
  select(c(County, year, Hired_workers)) %>%
  rename("county" = "County",
         "num_hired" = "Hired_workers")

# list parameters for NASS API query
params <- list(agg_level_desc = "county",
               state_name = "Idaho",
               year = c(2002, 2012, 2022),
               short_desc = c("Labor, hired - Number of workers"),
               domain_desc = "total")

# query NASS API
hired <- nassqs(params)

# clean hired workers data
hired_clean <- hired %>%
  mutate(county_name = str_to_title(county_name),
         # remove commas from numbers
         Value = as.numeric(str_remove_all(Value, ",")),
         # match years
         year = as.integer(year)-2) %>%
  group_by(county_name, year) %>%
  # add all hired worker for each year and county
  summarise(num_hired = sum(Value)) %>%
  rename("county" = "county_name") %>%
  # add 1990 data
  rbind(hired1990)

# read in interpolated private employment data
agsupport9712 <- read.csv("../data/raw_data/employment/efsy_panel_naics.csv") %>%
  # filter to Idaho and current years
  filter(fipstate == 16 & year %in% c(1997, 2002, 2012)) %>%
  # filter to ag support professions
  filter(naics12 %in% c(unique(.$naics12[str_starts(.$naics12, "1151")]),
                        unique(.$naics12[str_starts(.$naics12, "1152")]))) %>%
  mutate(fipscty = str_pad(fipscty, 3, pad="0"),
         GEOID = paste0(fipstate, fipscty)) %>%
  group_by(GEOID, year) %>%
  # add ag workers together
  summarise(ag_workers = sum(emp))

# pull CBP private employment data for 2022
agsupport2022 <- getCensus(name = "cbp",
                            vintage=2022,
                  vars = c("EMP", "NAICS2017"),
                  region = "county:*",
                  regionin = "state:16") %>%
  # filter to ag support professions
  filter(NAICS2017 %in% c("1151", "1152")) %>%
  # add GEOID and year labels
  mutate(GEOID = paste0(state, county),
         year = 2022) %>%
  group_by(GEOID, year) %>%
  # add ag workers together
  summarise(ag_workers = sum(EMP))

# combine private ag workers data
agsupport <- do.call(rbind, list(agsupport9712, agsupport2022)) %>%
  mutate(county = recode(GEOID, !!!GEOID_names))

# get population (more info in actors section)
pop1990 <- read.csv("../data/cencounts.csv") %>%
  select(pop1990, name) %>%
  filter(str_starts(name, "ID") & name != "ID Idaho") %>%
  mutate(name = str_remove(name, "ID "),
         name = str_remove(name, " County"))
pop2000 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "P001001",
                        year = 2000) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))
pop2010 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "P001001",
                        year = 2010) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))
pop2020 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "P1_001N",
                        year = 2020) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))

pop <- data.frame(county = c(pop1990$name,
                                  pop2000$NAME,
                                  pop2010$NAME,
                                  pop2020$NAME),
                            year = rep(seq(1990, 2020, 10), each = nrow(pop1990)),
                            pop = c(pop1990$pop1990,
                                    pop2000$value,
                                    pop2010$value,
                                    pop2020$value))

# join population and ag support data
agjobs_pop <- left_join(pop, agsupport, by = c("county", "year")) %>%
  # join on hired workers data
  left_join(hired_clean, by = c("county", "year")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  # add 0 for any county with no ag workers
  mutate(ag_workers = ifelse(is.na(ag_workers), 0, ag_workers),
         pop = as.integer(pop)) %>%
  # calculate number ag workers per 1000 people
  mutate(ag_support_per_1000 = sum(ag_workers, num_hired) / (pop/1000))

# clean and join to all resource units data
ru_data <- agjobs_pop %>%
  select(county, year, ag_support_per_1000) %>%
  right_join(ru_data, by = c("county", "year"))
```

```{r}

accomfood <- do.call(rbind, list(accomfood9010, accomfood2020)) %>%

# get population (more info in actors section)

  mutate(name = str_remove(name, "ID "),

pop2000 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "P001001",
                        year = 2000) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))
pop2010 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "P001001",
                        year = 2010) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))
pop2020 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "P1_001N",
                        year = 2020) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))

pop <- data.frame(county = c(pop1990$name,
                                  pop2000$NAME,
                                  pop2010$NAME,
                                  pop2020$NAME),
                            year = rep(seq(1990, 2020, 10), each = nrow(pop1990)),
                            pop = c(pop1990$pop1990,
                                    pop2000$value,
                                    pop2010$value,
                                    pop2020$value))

# combine population and workers data
accomfood_pop <- left_join(pop, accomfood, by = c("county", "year")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  # fill missing values with 0
  mutate(accom_food_workers = ifelse(is.na(accom_food_workers), 0, accom_food_workers),
         pop = as.integer(pop)) %>%
  # calculate accomdation and food workers per 1000 people
  mutate(accom_food_per_1000 = accom_food_workers / (pop/1000))

ru_data <- accomfood_pop %>%
  select(county, year, accom_food_per_1000) %>%
  right_join(ru_data, by = c("county", "year"))
```

### Urban / Residential

#### Median home value

Values for 2000-2020 are downloaded via API call using `tidycensus`. Values for 1990 were digitized from Table 51 of the 1990 Census of Housing Idaho (https://www2.census.gov/library/publications/decennial/1990/ch-1/ch-1-14.pdf).

Consumer price indices were retrieved from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (https://download.bls.gov/pub/time.series/cu/cu.data.12.USHousing). (Time series information here: https://download.bls.gov/pub/time.series/cu/)

```{r}
#| label: "median home value"

# to adjust for inflation, we need the consumer price index for each year
cpiu_housing_dec_1990 <- 131
cpiu_housing_dec_2000 <- 172.8
cpiu_housing_dec_2010 <- 216.823
cpiu_housing_dec_2020 <- 274.303

homeval1990 <- read.csv("../data/1990_US_Census_data.csv") %>%
  select(County, Year, Median_owner_occupied_housing_unit_value) %>%
  mutate(cpiu = cpiu_housing_dec_1990) %>%
  rename("county" = "County",
         "year" = "Year",
         "med_home_val" = "Median_owner_occupied_housing_unit_value")

homeval2000 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                             variables = "H076001",
                             year = 2000,
                             state = "ID") %>%
  mutate(county = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"),
         year = 2000,
         cpiu = cpiu_housing_dec_2000) %>%
  rename("med_home_val" = "value") %>%
  select(county, year, med_home_val, cpiu)
  

homeval2010 <- get_acs(geography = "county",
                       variables = "B25077_001",
                       year = 2010,
                       state = "ID") %>%
  mutate(county = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"),
         year = 2010,
         cpiu = cpiu_housing_dec_2010) %>%
  rename("med_home_val" = "estimate") %>%
  select(county, year, med_home_val, cpiu)

homeval2020 <- get_acs(geography = "county",
                       variables = "B25077_001",
                       year = 2020,
                       state = "ID") %>%
  mutate(county = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"),
         year = 2020,
         cpiu = cpiu_housing_dec_2020) %>%
  rename("med_home_val" = "estimate") %>%
  select(county, year, med_home_val, cpiu)

homevals <- rbind(homeval1990, homeval2000, homeval2010, homeval2020) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(cpiu_ratio = cpiu_housing_dec_2020 / cpiu,
         med_home_val_in_2020_USD = med_home_val * cpiu_ratio) %>%
  select(county, year, med_home_val_in_2020_USD)

ru_data <- left_join(ru_data, homevals, by = c("county", "year"))
```


## RU5 -- Number of units

### Agriculture

#### Number farms per unit area

Data for 2002-2022 are available through the USDA NASS API. Data for 1992 were digitized from https://agcensus.library.cornell.edu/census_parts/1992-idaho/, Chapter 2, Table 6.

```{r}
#| label: "number farms per unit area"

params <- list(agg_level_desc = "county",
               state_name = "Idaho",
               year = c(2002, 2012, 2022),
               short_desc = c("Farm operations - number of operations",
                              "Land area, incl non-ag - acres"),
               domain_desc = "total")

num_farms <- nassqs(params)

num_farms_1992 <- read.csv("../data/Farm_size_1925-1992.csv") %>%
  filter(Year == 1992 & Size == "all farms") %>%
  left_join(read.csv("../data/perc_land_in_farms_ID_counties_1925-2022.csv")) %>%
  mutate(farms_per_acre = Num_farms / Total_county_land_acres) %>%
  select(County, Year, farms_per_acre) %>%
  rename("county" = "County",
         "year" = "Year") %>%
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year-2))

# clean and join
ru_data <- num_farms %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(county_name, year),
              names_from = statisticcat_desc,
              values_from = Value) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(farms_per_acre = `OPERATIONS` / `AREA`) %>%
  rename("county" = "county_name") %>%
  mutate(county = str_to_title(county),
         year = as.numeric(year)) %>%
  select(c(county, year, farms_per_acre)) %>%
  mutate(year = (year-2)) %>%
  rbind(num_farms_1992) %>%
  right_join(ru_data, by=c("county", "year"))
```

### Natural Amenities

#### Recreation Units

The Protected Areas Database "was originally designed to support biodiversity assessments; however, its scope expanded in recent years to include all public and nonprofit held lands and waters." ([source](https://www.usgs.gov/programs/gap-analysis-project/pad-us-data-manual)). PAD-US 4.1 data were downloaded from https://www.usgs.gov/programs/gap-analysis-project/science/pad-us-data-download

The following land designations were considered recreation lands to calculate percent recreation land in this analysis: Recreation Management Area, National Monument, National Park, State Recreation Area, State Park, National Recreation Area, National Scenic or Historic Trail. Additional local designation terms related to recreation were added as well, as some state parks were misclassified as `LP` (local parks) in the `Des_Tp` (designation type) column.

We also use Euclidean distance to calculate distance to national parks and ski areas within 100km.

```{r}
#| label: "percent recreation lands - RU"

padus <- st_read("/vsizip/../data/raw_data/PADUS4_1Geodatabase.zip/PADUS4_1Geodatabase.gdb", 
                 layer = "PADUS4_1Combined_Proclamation_Marine_Fee_Designation_Easement") %>%
  filter(State_Nm %in% c("ID", "WA", "OR", "WY", "UT", "NV", "MT")) %>%
  filter(st_is_valid(.))

pad_rec <- padus %>%
  st_filter(st_transform(county_shapes, st_crs(.))) %>%
  filter(Des_Tp %in% c("REC", "NM", "NP", "SREC", "SP", "NRA", "NT") |
           Loc_Ds %in% c("State Park", "Recreation Reservoir", "National Recreation Trail", "Recreation Area", "National Recreation Area", "National Monument", "SREC", "REC", "SP", "National Park", "Designated - Recreational"))

pad_ski_np <- padus %>%
  filter(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Ski ") | Des_Tp == "NP" | str_detect(Unit_Nm, "National Park"))

pad_rec_years <- vector("list", length=4)
names(pad_rec_years) <- seq(1990, 2020, 10)

pad_rec_years <- mapply(function(list, year) {
  county_polys <- pad_rec %>% 
    filter(Date_Est <= year | is.na(Date_Est)) %>%
    st_intersection(., st_transform(county_shapes, st_crs(.))) %>%
    st_make_valid()
  county_polys <- county_polys[list(st_geometry_type(county_polys))[[1]] %in% c("POLYGON", "MULTIPOLYGON"),]
    
  county_polys <- county_polys %>%
    group_by(NAME) %>%
    dplyr::summarise() %>%
    st_make_valid()
}, list = pad_rec_years, year = seq(1990, 2020, 10), SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

rec_by_county_years <- lapply(pad_rec_years, function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(rec_area = st_area(.)) %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    left_join(st_drop_geometry(county_shapes)) %>%
    mutate(perc_rec = units::drop_units(rec_area / tot_area * 100))
})

# clean and join
ru_data <- bind_rows(rec_by_county_years, .id="year") %>%
  rename("county" = "NAME") %>%
  select("county", "year", "perc_rec") %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) %>%
  right_join(ru_data, by=c("county", "year")) %>%
  # convert NAs to 0% rec land
  mutate(perc_rec = ifelse(is.na(perc_rec), 0, perc_rec))
```

```{r}
# national parks within 100km
np_nn <- st_nearest_feature(st_transform(county_shapes, st_crs(pad_ski_np)),
                          subset(pad_ski_np, !str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Ski ")))
np_distance <- st_distance(st_transform(county_shapes, st_crs(pad_ski_np)),
                           subset(pad_ski_np, !str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Ski "))[np_nn,],
                           by_element = TRUE) %>%
  units::set_units("km") %>%
  cbind(county_shapes$NAME) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("county" = "V2",
         "dist_to_NP" = ".") %>%
  mutate(dist_to_NP = as.numeric(dist_to_NP))

# join
ru_data <- left_join(ru_data, np_distance, by = "county")
```

```{r}
# ski areas within 100km
counties_buff <- st_buffer(county_shapes, units::set_units(100, "km")) %>%
  st_transform(st_crs(pad_ski_np))

# manual date correction - when people started using the ski area
ski_areas <- subset(pad_ski_np, str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Ski")) %>%
  st_filter(counties_buff) %>%
  # https://skilookout.com/history-of-lookout
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Lookout Pass"), 1941, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://www.montanaliving.com/blogs/people/ski-visionaries-of-montana-discovery-basin
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Discovery Basin"), 1984, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://losttrail.com/about-lost-trail/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Lost Trail"), 1967, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://southwestmt.com/specialfeatures/this-is-montana/ski-areas/maverick-mountain/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Maverick Mountain"), 1946, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://visitmt.com/listing/turner-mountain
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Turner Mountain"), 1960, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://fremontcountyhistoricalsociety.org/article/bear-gulch-ski-basin
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Bear Basin"), 1939, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://fromboise.com/posts/the-history-of-bogus-basin
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Bogus Basin"), 1942, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://brundage.com/media/history/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Brundage Mountain"), 1961, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://www.grandtarghee.com/plan-your-trip/discover/about-targhee/history-of-targhee
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Grand Targhee"), 1966, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://www.jacksonhole.com/history
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Jackson Hole"), 1964, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://rexburgfun.com/kelly-canyon-ski-resort/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Kelly Canyon"), 1957, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://mccallskiheritagefoundation.org/mccall-ski-history/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Little Ski Hill"), 1937, Date_Est)) %>%
  # "Ski resort set for big season". Spokane Daily Chronicle. (Washington). Associated Press. November 23, 1951. p. 8.
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Magic Mountain"), 1951, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://www.idahostatejournal.com/news/local/tales-from-the-rock-local-riders-and-employees-recount-memories-as-pebble-creek-celebrates-75/article_ee54f6e0-d11e-11ee-bd6c-5b2de0909f20.html
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Pebble Creek"), 1949, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://www.kivitv.com/news/outdoors/pomerelle-mountain-resort-features-a-unique-mix-of-elevation-history-and-family-vibes
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Pomerelle"), 1940, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://snowkingmountain.com/discover-snow-king/snow-king-mountain-resort-history/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Snow King"), 1946, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://www.snowbasin.com/about/history/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Snowbasin"), 1940, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://soldiermountain.com/about/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Soldier Mountain"), 1947, Date_Est)) %>%
  # https://visitsunvalley.com/about-sun-valley/history/
  mutate(Date_Est = ifelse(str_detect(Unit_Nm, "Sun Valley"), 1936, Date_Est))

pad_ski_years <- vector("list", length=4)
names(pad_ski_years) <- seq(1990, 2020, 10)

pad_ski_years <- mapply(function(list, year) {
  # apply(st_intersects(counties_buff,
  #                     subset(ski_areas, (Date_Est <= year | is.na(Date_Est))),
  #                     sparse = FALSE),
  #                  MARGIN = 1,
  #                  FUN = sum) %>%
  #   cbind(county_shapes$NAME) %>%
  #   as.data.frame() %>%
  #   rename("county" = "V2",
  #          "ski_areas_100km" = ".") %>%
  #   mutate(ski_areas_100km = as.integer(ski_areas_100km))
  
  ski_nn <- st_nearest_feature(st_transform(county_shapes, st_crs(ski_areas)),
                          ski_areas)
  ski_distance <- st_distance(st_transform(county_shapes, st_crs(ski_areas)),
                           ski_areas[ski_nn,],
                           by_element = TRUE) %>%
  units::set_units("km") %>%
  cbind(county_shapes$NAME) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("county" = "V2",
         "dist_to_ski" = ".") %>%
  mutate(dist_to_ski = as.numeric(dist_to_ski))
  
  return(ski_distance)
}, list = pad_ski_years, year = seq(1990, 2020, 10), SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

# clean and join
ru_data <- bind_rows(pad_ski_years, .id="year") %>%
  select("county", "year", "dist_to_ski") %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) %>%
  right_join(ru_data, by=c("county", "year"))
```

### Residential

#### Number houses per unit area

Data for 2000-2020 were downloaded via `tidycensus`. Data for 1990 were digitized from https://www2.census.gov/library/publications/decennial/1990/cph-2/cph-2-14.pdf (available at https://www.census.gov/library/publications/1992/dec/cph-2.html)

```{r}
#| label: "number houses per unit area"

houses1990 <- read.csv("../data/1990_US_Census_data.csv")
houses2000 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "H001001",
                        year = 2000) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))
houses2010 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "H001001",
                        year = 2010) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))
houses2020 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "H1_001N",
                        year = 2020) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))

county_areas <- read.csv("../data/perc_land_in_farms_ID_counties_1925-2022.csv") %>%
  filter(Year >= 1990) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(Year-2)) %>%
  select(County, Year, Total_county_land_acres)

housing_units <- data.frame(county = c(houses1990$County,
                                       houses2000$NAME,
                                       houses2010$NAME,
                                       houses2020$NAME),
                            year = rep(seq(1990, 2020, 10), each = nrow(houses1990)),
                            housing_units = c(houses1990$Housing_Units,
                                              houses2000$value,
                                              houses2010$value,
                                              houses2020$value)) %>%
  left_join(county_areas,
            by = c("county" = "County",
                   "year" = "Year")) %>%
  mutate(housing_units_per_acre = housing_units / Total_county_land_acres) %>%
  select(county, year, housing_units_per_acre)

# join
ru_data <- left_join(ru_data, housing_units)
```

## RU6 -- Distinctive characteristics

### Agriculture

#### Farm sizes

2002-2022 data are downloaded from NASS API. Data for 1992 were digitized from https://agcensus.library.cornell.edu/census_parts/1992-idaho/, Chapter 2, Table 6. 

The range is described by size categories that add up to 100% of farms, so for these data, we use PCA scores that describe >75% of the variance rather than the raw data (following the methods of Aho et al., 2022).

```{r}
#| label: "farm sizes"

# farm sizes range
# list parameters
params <- list(state_alpha = "ID",
               agg_level_desc = "county",
               year = c(2002, 2012, 2022),
               commodity_desc = "Farm operations",
               short_desc = "Farm operations - number of operations",
               domain_desc = "area operated")
# retrieve
farm_sizes <- nassqs(params)
# save a backup copy
# write.csv(farm_sizes,
#           "../data/API_data_download_backup/farm_sizes.csv",
#           row.names = FALSE)

# clean
farm_sizes2 <- farm_sizes %>%
  # remove redundant categories
  filter(!(domaincat_desc %in% c("AREA OPERATED: (180 TO 219 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (220 TO 259 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (260 TO 499 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (50.0 TO 69.9 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (70.0 TO 99.9 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (100 TO 139 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (140 TO 179 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (1,000 OR MORE ACRES)"))) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(county_name, year),
              names_from = domaincat_desc,
              values_from = Value) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(total_farms = sum(c_across(`AREA OPERATED: (1,000 TO 1,999 ACRES)`:`AREA OPERATED: (500 TO 999 ACRES)`), na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(across(`AREA OPERATED: (1,000 TO 1,999 ACRES)`:`AREA OPERATED: (500 TO 999 ACRES)`,
                ~.x/total_farms*100))

# 1992 data
farm_sizes_1992 <- read.csv("../data/Farm_size_1925-1992.csv") %>%
  filter(Year == 1992) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c("County", "Year"),
              names_from = "Size",
              values_from = "Num_farms") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(across(`under 10 acres`:`over 2,000 acres`,
                ~.x/`all farms`*100)) %>%
  # create comparable categories
  mutate(`AREA OPERATED: (1,000 TO 1,999 ACRES)` = `1,000 to 1,999 acres`,
         `AREA OPERATED: (1.0 TO 9.9 ACRES)` = `under 10 acres`,
         `AREA OPERATED: (10.0 TO 49.9 ACRES)` = `10 to 49 acres`,
         `AREA OPERATED: (180 TO 499 ACRES)` = `180 to 219 acres` + `220 to 259 acres` + `260 to 499 acres`,
         `AREA OPERATED: (2,000 OR MORE ACRES)` = `over 2,000 acres`,
         `AREA OPERATED: (50 TO 179 ACRES)` = `50 to 69 acres` + `70 to 99 acres` + `100 to 139 acres` + `140 to 179 acres`,
         `AREA OPERATED: (500 TO 999 ACRES)` = `500 to 999 acres`) %>%
  rename("county_name" = "County",
         "year" = "Year")

# join
farm_sizes_all <- rbind(farm_sizes2[,1:9],
                        farm_sizes_1992[,c(1:2,16:22)]) %>%
  replace(is.na(.), 0)
  
# PCA
farm_sizes_pca <- prcomp(farm_sizes_all[,-c(1:2)])
summary(farm_sizes_pca)
#biplot(farm_sizes_pca)

# join components explaining >75% of variance
ru_data <- cbind(farm_sizes_all, farm_sizes_pca$x[,1:2]) %>%
  select(county_name, year, PC1, PC2) %>%
  rename("county" = "county_name",
         "farm_size_pc1" = "PC1",
         "farm_size_pc2" = "PC2") %>%
  mutate(county = str_to_title(county),
         year = as.numeric(year)-2) %>%
  right_join(ru_data, by=c("county", "year"))
```

Save resource units data:

```{r}
write.csv(ru_data,
          "../data/RU_data.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```

Data for 2000-2020 were downloaded via `tidycensus`. Data for 1990 were downloaded from https://www.nber.org/research/data/census-us-decennial-county-population-data-1900-1990.

```{r}
#| label: "population density"

pop1990 <- read.csv("../data/raw_data/cencounts.csv") %>%
  select(pop1990, name) %>%
  filter(str_starts(name, "ID") & name != "ID Idaho") %>%
  mutate(name = str_remove(name, "ID "),

                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "P001001",
                        year = 2000) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))
pop2010 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "P001001",
                        year = 2010) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))
pop2020 <- get_decennial(geography = "county",
                        state = "ID",
                        variables = "P1_001N",
                        year = 2020) %>%
  mutate(NAME = str_remove(NAME, " County, Idaho"))

pop_dens <- data.frame(county = c(pop1990$name,

                            year = rep(seq(1990, 2020, 10), each = nrow(pop1990)),
                            pop = c(pop1990$pop1990,
```
